arguments.sql_query:
WITH cv AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS index_date
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (312327, 4329847, 381316, 4310996)
  GROUP BY co.person_id
),
followup AS (
  SELECT cv.person_id, co.condition_concept_id
  FROM cv
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co
    ON co.person_id = cv.person_id
   AND co.condition_start_date > cv.index_date
   AND co.condition_start_date <= DATE(cv.index_date, '+90 day')
),
category AS (
  SELECT f.person_id, cat.concept_id AS cat_id, cat.concept_name AS cat_name
  FROM followup f
  JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = f.condition_concept_id
  JOIN omop.concept cat ON cat.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
  WHERE cat.vocabulary_id = 'SNOMED'
    AND cat.concept_class_id = 'Clinical Finding'
    AND ca.min_levels_of_separation BETWEEN 3 AND 6
)
SELECT cat_name, COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS n_patients
FROM category
GROUP BY cat_name
ORDER BY n_patients DESC
LIMIT 25;

arguments.title: Diagnoses in the 90 days after a first cardiovascular event
arguments.subtitle: Cohort: 82,851 patients with a first MI or stroke (OMOP EHR)
arguments.summary: Among 82,851 patients with a first myocardial infarction or stroke, the diagnoses recorded in the following 90 days cluster into a small set of interlinked cardiometabolic categories. **Hypertension** (26,290 patients), **hyperlipidemia** (17,915), **cardiac arrhythmia** (17,800, mostly atrial fibrillation), **recurrent/other cerebrovascular disease** (16,569), **renal disease** (13,376), **diabetes mellitus** (13,005) and **heart failure** (12,830) dominate.\n\nThese are not independent: in the biomedical knowledge graph the underlying diseases share large sets of associated genes, and seven genes — **ACE, AGT, REN, INS, IL6, CRP, ALB** — are associated with *all seven* conditions. This points to shared biology: the renin–angiotensin system (ACE/AGT/REN) driving hypertension, cardiac remodeling and renal disease; insulin/metabolic signaling (INS, DPP4, GLP1R) linking diabetes and atherosclerosis; and systemic inflammation (IL6, CRP, TNF, CCL2, ICAM1) as a common thread across all cardiometabolic sequelae.

Here's the answer to the clinical question.

## Most frequent diagnosis categories in the 90 days after a first CV event

Cohort: **82,851 patients** with a first MI or stroke. Distinct-patient counts in the (index, +90 day] window:

| Category | Patients |
|---|---|
| Hypertension | 26,290 |
| Hyperlipidemia | 17,915 |
| Cardiac arrhythmia (mostly AFib) | 17,800 |
| Cerebrovascular disease (recurrent) | 16,569 |
| Renal disease | 13,376 |
| Diabetes mellitus | 13,005 |
| Heart failure | 12,830 |

Top individual diagnoses: essential hypertension (24,082), hyperlipidemia (13,639), congestive heart failure (10,358), old MI (9,532), coronary atherosclerosis (9,345), atrial fibrillation (9,111), anemia (8,681), abnormal ECG, chest pain, type 2 diabetes, acute kidney injury, and cerebral infarction.

## How they are biologically related

These categories form one interconnected cardiometabolic cluster. In the knowledge graph the underlying diseases share large gene sets — hypertension↔type 2 diabetes (239 shared genes), CAD↔MI (163), and hypertension with CAD/MI/heart failure (~145–151). Seven genes are associated with **all seven** conditions: **ACE, AGT, REN, INS, IL6, CRP, ALB**.

Three shared mechanisms explain the co-occurrence:
- **Renin–angiotensin system** (ACE, AGT, REN, EDN1) — links hypertension, cardiac remodeling/heart failure, and renal disease.
- **Metabolic/insulin signaling** (INS, DPP4, GLP1R, APOB, FTO) — links diabetes with atherosclerosis and hyperlipidemia.
- **Systemic inflammation & thrombosis** (IL6, CRP, TNF, CCL2, ICAM1, F2, F3) — a common driver across all cardiometabolic sequelae.
